test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Walking at (5)/(7) of his normal speed, Manish is 20 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed ratio (New : Normal) = 5 : 7 → Time ratio (New : Normal) = 7 : 5.

Difference in time units = 7 − 5 = 2 units.

Given 2 units = 20 minutes → 1 unit = 10 minutes.

Usual time (5 units) = 5 × 10 = 50 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c40c0244fee48e0900104cf60b7a9349ba5fe61def14d046b557c61d0fab58b.png] 

**Given:** New Speed = 5/7 × Normal Speed; Delay = 20 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Let Usual Speed = S and Usual Time = T.

⇒ Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = 5/7 S, New Time = T + 20

⇒ S × T = (5/7 S) × (T + 20)

⇒ T = 5/7 × (T + 20)

⇒ 7T = 5T + 100

⇒ 2T = 100

⇒ T = 50 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

If a person travels at a/b of their usual speed, the new time taken is b/a of the usual time.

General Formula for Late/Early

Usual Time = (Late time × a) ÷ (b − a) where new speed is a/b of usual speed.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x + y).</p
